subject: 2026-11-15-effort-drilldown-install

findings.title: T-10 cannot pass its tests before T-11 builds the memory section
quotes: Build the memory section from front matter and wire it into `show`
findings.fix: add T-11 to T-10's `Depends on:` (or move T-11 before T-10).

sources.situation: a worker takes T-10 after T-9, as the file orders them, and T-11 has not run yet. `show` has no `memory` key, so TC-25's assert that the output has the keys `timeline`, `juries`, `tasks`, `cost`, `memory` fails. TC-34 (which reads the memory section) fails the same way.

findings.reason: T-10 depends on T-4, T-8 and T-9, not T-11. TC-25 and TC-34 need a non-error `memory` key, and only T-11 builds it. TC-26, the only test T-1 owns, covers error cases only, so nothing else supplies the key.
findings.note: T-10 now depends on T-11 too

findings.title: T-5 is tested against sections that T-5 does not build
quotes: Build the timeline section from history
`juries` is a list holding the `spec` gate; `tasks` is a list; `memory` is a list.
findings.fix: move TC-5 to a later task that builds the other sections (T-10 or T-11), or have TC-5 assert only the timeline and juries-free parts. Replace T-3 in T-5's dependencies with what the timeline actually needs.

sources.situation: T-5 builds only the timeline and wires it into `show`. TC-5, which T-5 lists under `Test:`, asserts that `juries` holds the spec gate, that `tasks` and `memory` are lists, and that `cost` is an error object. Only T-7, T-8, T-10 and T-11 produce those sections, and T-5 depends on none of them. Run as written, T-5's test cannot pass. T-5's dependency on T-3 (a pane task) is also not needed for CLI timeline work.

findings.reason: T-5 lists TC-5 and depends on T-1 and T-3. TC-5 asserts that `juries` holds the spec gate, that `tasks` and `memory` are lists, and that `cost` is an error object. Those sections come from T-7, T-8, T-10 and T-11, which run later. T-3 is a pane task and the timeline build doesn't need it.
findings.note: Fix it: move TC-5 to the cost task (T-10) via a change request to the plan; human approved the change request

findings.title: T-13 owns TC-31, whose skill half is written by T-14
quotes: Test: TC-20, TC-21, TC-22, TC-23, TC-31, TC-36
the skill's mods step holds exactly one question (one line ending `?` whose options are the two commands).
findings.fix: move the skill assertion of TC-31 to T-14's `Test:`, or list TC-31 under T-14 and keep only its mods_dir and local-scope asserts under T-13.

sources.situation: T-13's files are `src/nio/hooks.py`, `src/nio/cli.py` and `tests/test_hooks.py`, with no SKILL.md. T-13 must pass TC-31, which includes an assert on `skills/install/SKILL.md`. The worker of T-13 cannot edit that file, and T-14 (which does) runs after T-13. TC-31 fails on the skill half for the whole of T-13.

findings.reason: T-13 lists TC-31 and its Files list has no `skills/install/SKILL.md`. TC-31 reads that skill and asserts the one-question step, which only T-14 writes. T-14 runs after T-13, so TC-31 fails on its skill half during T-13.
findings.note: TC-31 moved from T-13 to T-14, which writes the skill step

findings.title: T-1 names per-section isolation, but nothing tests it and the sections do not exist yet
quotes: with its error cases and per-section isolation
Each of the five section keys holds the value of CT-3, CT-4, CT-5, CT-6 or CT-7, or `{"error": "<text>"}` when building that section raised (FR-13)
findings.fix: state in T-1 what each section key holds until its task lands (for example `[]` or `"-"`), and give T-1 a test for the isolation wrapper, or move "per-section isolation" to T-5.

sources.situation: T-1's only test is TC-26, which covers the error cases. Per-section isolation is tested in TC-5 under T-5, and T-1 cannot build section values for CT-3 to CT-7, which come in later tasks. A worker of T-1 does not know what the five keys hold, or whether a section's `try` must already exist, so two workers could ship different isolation rules.

findings.note: T-1 states each section key is an empty placeholder until its task fills it; isolation is proven by TC-5 (no new test: the plan's TC list is fixed)

findings.title: T-3 and T-6 both own the timeline drawing and the same tests
quotes: draw the timeline, Back, errors, old-nio message, no actions
Pane draws the timeline rows and failed-review reasons from real `flow show` output
Test: TC-2, TC-6, TC-27, TC-28, TC-35, TC-37
Test: TC-2, TC-6, TC-27, TC-28, TC-29
findings.fix: give timeline rendering to one task. Drop TC-2, TC-6, TC-27 and TC-28 from the other, and drop TC-29 from T-6 (T-2 owns it).

sources.situation: T-3 says it draws the timeline and lists TC-2, TC-6, TC-27 and TC-28. T-6 says it draws the timeline rows and failed-review reasons and lists the same four tests. A worker of T-6 cannot tell what is left to build after T-3, and the two tasks may edit the same rendering code twice. TC-29 is owned by T-2 and is listed again under T-6.

findings.note: T-3 is the one task that draws the timeline; T-6 drops TC-6/27/28/29 and only adds the failed-review reason lines, re-checking TC-2 on T-5's output (TC-2 must stay in Foundation per the plan's build order)
